title: Stop the API quota from serving calls nobody paid for

blocks.text: The public API sells calls in packs. Billing tops a client up through `grant`, and every request thread calls `tryUse` before it serves a call. In last month's traffic spike two things went wrong: clients who bought a pack at the same moment as an automatic renewal got only one of the two, and clients with a single call left were served two or three calls for it.
The quotas already live in a `ConcurrentHashMap`. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Quotas.java`:

items: `grant(client, calls)`: add the calls to what the client has left;
`tryUse(client)`: take one call if there is one, and say whether it did.

blocks.text: When you're done, every top-up counts however many arrive together, a client's last call is served once, and the quota never goes below zero. About eight lines in total.
The tests make two calls interleave the same way on every run, through the map the class is given.

cases.says: top-ups add up, each served call takes one from the quota, and a client with nothing left, or never granted anything, is refused
when two top-ups for one client interleave, the quota grows by both
when two requests interleave on a client's last call, exactly one gets it and the quota ends at zero

origin.section: A Synchronized Wrapper Makes Each Call Atomic, Not a Sequence of Calls

concepts: A synchronized wrapper, like a ConcurrentHashMap, makes each call atomic but not a get followed by a put; a read-modify-write must be one call such as merge or compute.
